subject: اللغة الإنجليزية
outcomes: Explain why communication and expressing feelings matter
Recognise the skills of a good communicator
Use tips to keep a conversation going

tf.s: Negative feelings that stay inside can make you unhappy or angry.
tf.why: Right! That is why we should express our feelings.

tf.s: 'Pent-up' feelings are feelings that are held in.
tf.why: Correct! The text says feelings can get trapped inside your head.
Laila is the better communicator; she gives extra information and asks a question.

tf.s: Answering only 'yes' or 'no' keeps a conversation going.
tf.why: Give more information so the conversation can continue.

tf.s: Making eye contact is a tip for a good conversation.
tf.why: Eye contact shows you are listening.

tf.s: Saying 'whatever' shows that you are interested.
Taking turns is important in a conversation.
tf.why: Good! Both speakers should get a chance to talk.

tf.s: The writer advises keeping your problems a secret from everyone.
tf.why: The writer says talking to someone about a problem makes you feel better.

tf.s: Asking a follow-up question can keep a conversation going.
tf.why: Yes! A related question shows interest.

boxes.q: What two things does communication involve?
Who communicates better in the interviews?
boxes.why: Laila gives extra information and asks a question back.
'How about you?' asks the other person to share too.
'Really?' shows you want to hear more.

boxes.q: How can you show you are listening?
boxes.why: Nodding shows the speaker you are listening.

boxes.q: A good follow-up question for 'I went to Salalah last week' is:
boxes.why: A related question keeps the talk going.

boxes.q: What can happen if you don't express negative feelings?
o: you may not sleep or relax
boxes.why: Trapped feelings can make you unhappy.

boxes.q: Which is a good title for the text?
boxes.why: The title should show the main idea of the text.

boxes.q: Which phrase is a friendly greeting?
boxes.why: 'Nice to see you!' is one of the Soundbites.

hunt.q: Sound that shows you are listening
Movement that shows you are listening

mcq.q: Why is it important to express our feelings?
o: Negative feelings can get trapped inside and make us unhappy or angry
mcq.why: Sharing feelings helps us feel better.

mcq.q: What does the writer advise if you have pent-up feelings?
mcq.why: Sharing a problem makes you feel better.

mcq.q: Which is one of the five tips for a good conversation?
mcq.why: Related questions keep the conversation going.

mcq.q: Which phrase is one of the Soundbites?
mcq.why: Phrases like 'That's interesting' keep a chat friendly.

mcq.q: Your friend says, 'I like swimming.' What is the best reply to keep the conversation going?
mcq.why: Show interest and ask a follow-up question.

mcq.q: The teacher asks Ahmed, 'Do you have any brothers?' Which answer is best?
o: Yes, I have two. They both go to my school. How about you?
mcq.why: Add details and a question back to keep talking.

mcq.q: In a conversation, your partner speaks and you want to show you are listening. What should you do?
o: Make eye contact and say 'mm' or 'really?'
Start a new topic at once
mcq.why: Eye contact and small words show interest.

mcq.q: Why is Laila a better communicator than Ahmed?
o: She gives extra information, adds comments and asks a question
mcq.why: Extra information and questions keep a conversation going.

mcq.q: A conversation where one person only says 'yes' and 'no' is not successful. Why?
o: It does not keep the conversation going

mcq.q: The text calls communication 'a two-sided relationship'. What does this mean?
o: Both people must talk and listen
People must sit on two sides
mcq.why: Good communication needs talking and listening from both sides.
